correctness.rationale: Affine normalization gives explicit strict sign descriptions of all simplex vertex tangent-cone interiors. Those interiors are pairwise disjoint. Tangent cones of Cartesian products factor, so one direction illuminates at most one product vertex. The vertex lower bound therefore applies both ordinarily and fractionally; one interior direction per vertex gives the matching upper bound because illuminating a face vertex also illuminates every point of that face. The fixed-dimension gap follows from the sharp elementary inequalities d+1<=2^d and d+1<=3*2^(d-2) for d>=2.
risks: The finite checker is only diagnostic; the theorem rests on the exact tangent-cone argument.

Livshyts--Tikhomirov's open full text proves a strict local result near the cube but not an exact Cartesian-product formula. Candidate-specific semantic and exact-object searches under product of simplices, polysimplex, prism, Cartesian product, ordinary illumination, fractional illumination, and vertex-count formulations found no theorem implying the accepted claim.

value.rationale: Products of simplices form a canonical all-dimensional simple-polytope class ranging from a simplex to the cube. Determining both ordinary and fractional illumination exactly on the whole class gives a structural benchmark for the Levi--Hadwiger problem. The sharp nonparallelotope maximum 3*2^(n-2), attained exactly by a triangle times a cube, strengthens the qualitative cube-uniqueness expectation by a uniform 25 percent gap inside this natural class.
risks: The theorem is a class result and does not address general convex bodies outside products of simplices.
